title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes Grothendieck axiomatises a structure (M, 𝔉, ≤, ≪). M is a set of 'elements' or 'pieces'. 𝔉 is a set of 'figures' F, each with an underlying set F̃ ⊂ M. The relation X ≪ Y is read as 'X lies in the shadow (Omb) of Y', with Omb(Y) = {X : X ≪ Y}, and it is extended to figures. Each figure F carries a map φ_F sending X (in the shadow of F) to the smallest element of F̃ that 'covers' X, i.e. the least Y ∈ F̃ with X ≪ Y. So φ_F is a reflection or closure-type operator.

On p.26 the Proposition says that G ≪ F is equivalent to the existence of a map f: G̃ → F̃ compatible with the φ's, as in diagram (1.42). The candidate map is f(X) = least element of F̃ with X ≪ f(X), and it is shown to be increasing. p.26 also introduces the 'infinitely interior' relation (1.48). X °≪ Y means that X ∈ Omb(Y)° = Omb(Y) minus the union of Omb(Y') over Y' < Y. Equivalently, X ≪ Y, and Y is minimal among the Y' ≤ Y with X ≪ Y'.

This page:
(1) Grothendieck sees that the needed compatibility, i.e. the Corollary on p.26 (X ≪ G ≪ F; least element of G^X, then least element of F^{X'}, equals least element of F^X), cannot be derived from the existing axioms. He therefore posits Axiom AE7: X °≪ Y °≪ Z ⇒ X °≪ Z, i.e. the infinitely-interior relation is transitive. AE7 gives the ⇒ direction of the Proposition.
(2) Converse: suppose f as in (1.42) exists and take X ∈ G̃. Then φ_G(X) = X tautologically, so by condition (6) Y := f(X) = φ_F(X). Hence Y is the least element of F̃ with X ≪ Y. So every X ∈ G̃ is ≪ some Y ∈ F̃, which is condition (C4), G̃ ≪ F̃. QED. He remarks that the monotonicity of f was not used.
(3) He starts a Corollary: a criterion for an inclusion of shadows Omb F ⊂ Omb G (equivalently F ≪ G), stated also between some 'Mod/Comb' objects attached to F and G. The tentative sufficient condition is F ≪ G together with: the equivalence relation on Omb F defined by φ_F (X ~ X' iff φ_F(X) = φ_F(X')) is finer than the one induced from Omb G. A marginal note retracts this ('Ce n'est pas vrai, il faut que … R_F … plus petite'). It notes the condition is false as stated and that the relation R_F must instead be smaller, i.e. the comparison of equivalence relations goes the other way or must be strengthened.

On p.28 this whole structure is read as an axiomatisation of 'figures ensemblistes' Fig(M) ⊂ 𝔓𝔓(M). The data (𝔉, ≤, ≪) are equivalent to a set M with a subset 𝔉_M ⊂ Fig(M) satisfying conditions C1–C7. The problem served is building an intrinsic combinatorial/order-theoretic axiomatics for 'figures' in a tame-topology-like analysis situs.
errors: The Corollary as first formulated (sufficiency of F ≪ G plus φ_F-equivalence finer than the induced one) is retracted by Grothendieck himself in the margin as 'not true'. The correct condition (R_F 'smaller', a direction or strengthening) is left unresolved on this page.

AE7 is introduced as a new axiom rather than a consequence. Transitivity of ≪ alone gives X ≪ Z, but not the minimality of Z required for X °≪ Z, so an axiom is indeed needed. This is a gap Grothendieck fills by fiat rather than an error.

The converse direction uses only condition (6) applied to φ_G(X) = X. The tautology φ_G(X) = X for X ∈ G̃ requires X ≪ X (reflexivity), which is presumably among the earlier axioms but is not restated here.

ideas.what: Relation 'infinitely interior' X °≪ Y (X in the shadow of Y but in no strictly smaller Y'), and the axiom that it is transitive (AE7)
ideas.modern_name: Minimal-cover / 'way-below'-like relation on a poset with a covering relation; transitivity axiom on an interior relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Order theory (e.g. way-below relation in continuous lattices, Scott 1970s), no direct analogue
ideas.where_published: Unpublished Montpellier notes (cote 156-6); Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the 'topologie modérée' programme without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Characterisation of G ≪ F by existence of a map G̃ → F̃ compatible with the reflection operators φ_G, φ_F (monotonicity automatic/unused)
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of reflective subposets / closure operators (Galois connection)

ideas.what: Comparison of shadows Omb F ⊂ Omb G via the equivalence relations induced by φ_F (fibres of the reflection)
ideas.modern_name: Refinement of partitions / kernel of a retraction

missed.claim: The correct criterion for Omb F ⊂ Omb G in terms of the equivalence relations R_F, R_G is left open after Grothendieck retracts his first formulation. It is part of the larger unpublished 1986 axiomatics of 'figures' (conditions C1–C7, AE axioms), which has never been worked out in the literature.
missed.quote: Ce n'est pas vrai, il faut que la relation R_F soit plus petite
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as a minor piece of the reconstruction of Grothendieck's 1986 analysis situs / tame topology axiomatics. The specific lemma is elementary order theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine step of order-theoretic bookkeeping: an extra transitivity axiom, the easy converse of a proposition, and a corollary retracted in the margin. Its interest is only as part of the largely unexplored 1986 analysis situs axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: 'Umb' should read 'Omb' (ombre/shadow), consistent with p.26: 'Omb F ⊂ Omb G'.
The first Corollary line reads roughly 'Mod.../Comb(F) ≪ ...Comb(G)' (compare 'Mod(F)' on p.28), not clearly 'Umb(F) ≪ Umb(G)'.
'tant que φ_G(X) = X' is better read as 'sait que φ_G(X) = X (tautologique)'.
The marginal note runs vertically at bottom left and reads approximately 'Ce n'est pas vrai, il faut que la relation R_F soit plus petite' (partly illegible).
'moyennant (6)' is correct; the struck-out text is 'on a donc', replaced by 'soit'.
